judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (ii) — costs 'capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' — is an open counterfactual test with no standard of timeliness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a revision of Agreement 7.7.2, whose unrevised text also appears in the instrument, so the two versions must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a proviso about absence of collectible insurance; the terms are specific though layered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It revises Agreement 7.7.3, which appears unrevised elsewhere, and depends on insurance requirements that Article 16 leaves blank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of fee-covered items closing with 'estimating/project purchasing costs and expenses', and the sweeping 'none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7' invites an ejusdem generis fight over its edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries the number of the Agreement's 8.1.8 (costs exceeding the Guaranteed Maximum Price) while saying something entirely different, and it contradicts 7.5.4's reimbursement of telephone, postage and facsimile costs and 7.6.6's data processing costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear notice-and-opportunity mechanism with a stated period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Agreement 9.1's default rule that cash discounts otherwise accrue to the Contractor, narrowing but not contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' is a subjective standard with no reasonableness qualifier in the chapeau.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears the same number as the Agreement's own 12.1.4, which imposes a different set of substantiation requirements, so two provisions share one designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed itemisation of what the statement must show; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1.7 and with 9.6.2.1's joint-payment mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires lien waivers 'establishing payment or satisfaction' for amounts included in the current application without saying whether the waivers are conditional or unconditional — a recurring source of argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties into Addendum 12.2.2's lien-free title endorsement condition and 12.2.1's Notice of Completion, which are consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all — 'such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' — following two specific items, which is the classic general-after-specific structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the Agreement's 12.1.4 catch-all and creates no separate inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retainage is fixed at five percent and the fee computation covers both rate and fixed-sum cases; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the Agreement's 12.1.7.3, which states retainage as 'N/A percent', so the document contains two versions of the same subparagraph with different numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single objective condition tied to publication and recordation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and dovetails with Addendum 12.2.2's recordation-based deadline, but sits against 12.2.3's Architect-certificate sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whichever is earlier' compares a recordation date with a lien-free endorsement date, either of which may never occur, leaving the trigger for final payment uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's 12.2.2 fixes final payment at 30 days after the Architect's final Certificate, and 12.2.3 builds a certificate-based sequence, so two different final-payment triggers coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Naming 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' leaves three alternative representatives without saying who binds the Owner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 says the Owner's authorized representative 'is Mary Williamson' while listing three people who may act, so the identity of the representative is stated three different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A chapeau reciting survival and materiality; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fills the Agreement's blank 14.6 and adds to representations elsewhere, without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Financially solvent' and 'sufficient working capital' are judgment terms, but the representation is a factual warranty rather than a scope term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses Contractor solvency; A201 2.2.1 imposes the mirror obligation on the Owner.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficient experience and competence' is a soft measure inside an otherwise plain capability warranty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Addendum Article 2's skilled-staff requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All necessary governmental and public and quasi-public authorities' is broad, but licensing status is an objective fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing licensing provision appears in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional site-visit representation with defined content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates A201 1.5.2's execution representation, an overlap that points the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-identifying and precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the Agreement's 15.1.1 and is consistent with Article 1's enumeration requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the edition and the modifying document plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's own 15.1.2 describes 'the 1991 edition' of A201-1997, so this revision is needed to cure a mismatch in the enumeration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporation of 'Articles 1 through 14 inclusive' is a bounded and definite reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 provides that the Agreement governs any inconsistency with other Contract Documents, so the scope of this wholesale incorporation must be read against that precedence rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Modify, change, delete from, and add to' followed by a survival rule for unaltered provisions is workable but requires judgment about what counts as altered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a third layer of precedence alongside Agreement Article 1 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1, and several supplements duplicate rather than cleanly replace Agreement provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wherever in the Contract Documents a matter requires notice to ... the Architect' sweeps across the whole instrument, and the disclaimer of responsibility 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner' is broadly drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grafts an Owner consent requirement onto every Architect function in A201, including certification under 9.4 and initial decisions under 4.4, which sits awkwardly with the Architect's independent role in those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Better quality or greater quantity', 'more stringent requirement' and 'either or both' give no rule for choosing between the two limbs and are inherently comparative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 says that where the other Contract Documents are inconsistent with the Agreement, the Agreement governs; this clause instead resolves all inconsistencies in favour of more work as the Architect interprets — two different conflict rules in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise drawing-precedence rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.2.1.1's general scheme; no Drawings are enumerated, but that bears on 15.1.5 rather than here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The flat bar on 'extra charge or compensation ... on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated on the Drawings' is absolute and one-sided in drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against A201 3.2 and 4.3.7 claim rights and against the change-order pricing machinery in Addendum 6.5, which contemplates payment for refinements as the design develops.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor change' is undefined here and 'sufficiently detailed drawings' supplies no standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.4 gives the Architect authority to order minor changes without cost or time effect, while Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 says changes may only be by Change Order, so three provisions govern the same ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence names a single authorized representative and the next names three people who may act, an internal tension in two adjoining sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 give two further formulations of who the Owner's representative is, and 14.5 requires notice before any change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day cure period with a defined deduction remedy; clear enough on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 2.4.1, reproduced in this instrument, requires a second seven-day notice before the Owner may act, so the revised and unrevised versions state different cure procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Detailed timetable of all activities and events' and the deeming of the Schedule into the Contract Documents 'as it is developed' leave the Schedule's contractual force uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 1.1.2 says the Contract may be amended only by Modification and Agreement Article 1 keys the Contract Documents to the Article 15 enumeration, yet this clause admits a document created later without either step.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Following completion of pre-construction services' and the three named design phases fix a sequence, but the clause makes every cost estimate 'part of the Contract Documents' without saying what contractual effect the estimate has.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 6.5 sets up a different pre-construction pricing regime (Preliminary Budget, Itemized Schedule of Values, Change Orders), and A201 1.1.2 permits amendment only by Modification, so three provisions describe how prices become binding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific submission and warranty requirement with an identifiable trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.12 and with Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's Owner-consent overlay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed pleading requirement for time claims; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements A201 4.3.7 without displacing its notice periods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled and the notion of delays with 'concurrent or interrelated effects' is left undefined, so what is barred is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies A201 4.3.7 and 8.3.1 extensions of time; the direction is consistent even if the wording is loose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars any claim based on 'course of conduct or dealings', 'express or implied acceptance of alterations or additions' and unjust enrichment, subject only to two cross-referenced exceptions — a sweeping, one-sided exclusion whose reach against extra-work claims is exactly what parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the cost-reimbursement structure of Articles 5 and 7, with Addendum 6.5's fast-track procedure in which prices are refined and Change Orders issued after the Work is under way, and with Supplementary Condition 3.10.5's later cost estimates that 'become part of the Contract Documents'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including, but not limited to' combines an accord with an open-ended list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 7.1.3.1's change-order-only rule but sits against 6.4's equitable fee adjustment and the Addendum's iterative pricing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary' and 'in their sole discretion' are strong but definite; the three no-privity disclaimers are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides other payment provisions by its own terms, which is a coordinated rather than conflicting drafting choice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Received and accepted by the Owner' gives the Owner an unqualified acceptance right over final certification, without a reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.1 and 12.2.3 make the final Certificate turn on the Architect's judgment and the accountants' report, so this adds an Owner veto to that sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear exclusion coupled with a waiver-of-subrogation requirement by cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 16 leaves insurance limits blank, so the required policies to which this refers are not specified anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All reasonable costs ... properly attributable thereto' is a familiar and bounded formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 'insurance required under Article 11' at a time when Agreement Article 16 states no limits, leaving the required coverage undefined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is headed 'construction costs to be reimbursed include' and then says the cost of hand tools 'shall be borne by the Contractor' before adding a 5% payroll surcharge, and the tool list is expressly non-exhaustive ('include, but are not limited to ... etc.') — both a self-contradiction and an open list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.5.1 makes such hand tools a direct reimbursable cost and 8.1.5 excludes rental costs except under 7.5.2, so the flat percentage substitute cannot be squared with Article 7's itemised scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed 1% formula applied to labour and subcontractor costs; arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract', which a flat percentage may exceed or fall short of.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All direct costs' is undefined and the list of vendor costs treated as 'Subcontract' costs is expressly open-ended ('including; rubbish hauling ... etc.'), so the exempt category has no fixed boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'related to the Work' without this carve-out, so the two set the tax base differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard definitional list closed by an express exclusion of unenumerated bidding documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 gives a slightly different list and a precedence rule, and Article 15's enumeration leaves Drawings and Specifications blank, so what is actually a Contract Document is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear integration and no-privity language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its rule that the Contract 'may be amended or modified only by Modification' is hard to square with Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5, which make later schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents automatically.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but standard definition of the Work tied to the Contract Documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the Drawings and Specifications are not enumerated, the definition's referent is thin, but the definition itself is consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definitional provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's identification of the Project.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A descriptive definition with an illustrative list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.5 enumerates no Drawings and dates them 'N/A', so the defined term has no identified content in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A descriptive definition of written requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.4 lists no Specifications and refers to a Project Manual whose date is blank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May include' makes the definition permissive but that is deliberate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 15.1.3 and 15.1.4 refer to a Project Manual that is not dated or identified, so the definition has no referent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably inferable from them as being necessary to produce the indicated results' is the classic scope phrase that construction parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 resolves inconsistencies in favour of greater quantity while Agreement Article 1 gives the Agreement precedence, and Agreement 5.2.6 prices only development 'reasonably inferable' — three overlapping scope rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and definite disclaimer about specification organisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 10's subcontracting scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It imports 'well-known technical or construction industry meanings' without identifying them, which is a rule about meaning rather than a determinate term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports rather than conflicts with the definitions in 1.1 and the Exhibits' trade terminology.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical capitalisation convention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision turns on it in a contested way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is itself about omitted modifiers such as 'all' and 'any', so it acknowledges but does not itself create indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an interpretive aid consistent with the rest of Article 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences with a simple fallback of Architect identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many of the Contract Documents here — Exhibits, the schedules deemed attached under 3.10.4 — are unsigned, so the identification mechanism carries weight but does not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional deemed representation on execution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 14.6(d) contains a near-identical site-visit representation, an overlap in the same direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but specific allocation of copyright and permitted uses, with express carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing intellectual property provision appears; 7.6.5 addresses royalties separately and consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription is badly broken, so the sentence about furnishing record legal title within fifteen days cannot be read continuously as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relates to Agreement 4.1's provision for Owner time to file mortgages and mechanic's lien notices, which was left blank, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' is an undefined standard and the clause makes it a 'condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work', which is strong medicine on soft wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article 12's payment machinery and Addendum 6.5's Owner termination right, but no provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear allocation with an express carve-out for permits under 3.7.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees a reimbursable Cost of the Work, which is consistent with the Contractor bearing them in the first instance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reliance on Owner-furnished survey information subject to exercising 'proper precautions' is a familiar balanced formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for verifying measurements at the site, which cuts against reliance on Owner-furnished data.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and 'any other information or services relevant to the Contractor's performance' are open but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 3 obliges the Owner to furnish and approve information in a timely manner, pointing the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably necessary' copies free of charge; a small, bounded obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Project Manual or Drawings are identified in Article 15, which thins the obligation but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently fails' is elastic, though the remedy and its limits are spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 2.4.1 and with Supplementary Condition 2.4.1's shortened cure procedure without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-stage seven-day notice procedure and 'reasonable cost of correcting such deficiencies' are detailed and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.4.1 revises this paragraph to delete the second notice, yet the original text remains in the instrument, so two different cure procedures appear for the same remedy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional sentence identifying the Contractor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's identification of Metzler Contracting Co. LLC and with 14.4's representative provision.
